source_text: Nam cum Apostolus pronuntiat: Gratia autem ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n160] , et hoc tu dicis in parvulis quidem non posse constare, in illis autem, qui iam perfectae aetatis sunt, solis ideo impleri, quia ad unum illud alia quoque motu propriae voluntatis addiderint, confiteris sine dubio diversam esse operationem gratiae pro diversitate venientium. In his quippe, qui motu propriae voluntatis utuntur, suppetit ei materia gloriandi, quia ex multis criminibus in iustificationem, quos adoptarit, educit; in parvulis autem secundum te ieiunius, angustius, exilius nec virtute magna nec medicina idonea nec honestate salva nec pudore securo unum illud peccatum se promittit auferre, quod nec debuit imputare, et ex hoc uno, quos liberat, in iustificationem conatur emittere.
pass_a_gloss: For when the Apostle pronounces: But grace from many offenses into justification, and you say that this indeed cannot stand in little children, but in those who are already of perfect age is fulfilled only for this reason, because they have added to that one also others by a motion of proper will, you confess without doubt that the operation of grace is diverse according to the diversity of those coming. For in these who use a motion of proper will there is at hand for it matter of glorying, because from many crimes into justification it leads out those whom it has adopted; but in little children according to you more fasting, more narrowly, more poorly, neither with great virtue nor with a fit medicine nor with honesty safe nor with shame secure it promises that it will take away that one sin, which it ought not even to have imputed, and from this one it tries to send out those whom it frees into justification.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: For the apostle declares, ‘But grace is from many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16). You say this cannot hold for infants but is fulfilled only in adults, because by the movement of their own will they have added other sins to that one. You therefore undoubtedly confess that grace operates differently according to the differences among those who approach it. In those who exercise their own will, it finds material for glory, since it leads those it adopts from many crimes into justification. But in infants, according to you, in a leaner, narrower, poorer fashion—with no great power, no adequate medicine, no intact honor, and no secure modesty—it promises to remove that one sin which it should not even have imputed, and tries to send those it frees from that one sin into justification.

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
